config.ompPath.description: Path to the omp CLI binary (oh-my-pi). Defaults to `omp` resolved via PATH (~/.bun/bin is added automatically).
config.language.description: Language of the chat interface. Independent of the VS Code display language, so the editor can stay English while the chat is Russian. Command titles and these setting descriptions still follow VS Code itself.
config.language.enumDescriptions.0: Follow the VS Code display language
config.customProviders.markdownDescripti: Custom model providers, same shape as the `providers:` map in `~/.omp/agent/models.yml`. Merged into models.yml before each agent start. Example: `{"akemi": {"baseUrl": "http://host:8000/v1", "api": "openai-completions", "apiKey": "sk-...", "models": [{"id": "akemi-1", "name": "Akemi", "contextWindow": 128000, "maxTokens": 32000}]}}`
config.defaultModel.markdownDescription: Model to select after the agent starts, as `provider/modelId` (fuzzy matched), e.g. `akemi/akemi-1` or `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`. Empty = keep the agent's default.
config.verifyModels.markdownDescription: Before offering a model, send it one throwaway request (`ping`, thinking off, no tools) through a separate session-less agent and keep only the models that answer. Hides models whose credentials are stale or whose subscription does not cover them. Verdicts are cached for 12 hours; refresh them from the model picker's "Re-check subscriptions".
config.hideStartupNotices.markdownDescri: Hide the agent's internal startup notices (`xd://: mounted …`, `inspect_image is now hidden …`). Warnings and errors are always shown; suppressed notices still go to the "OMP Code" output channel.
config.resumeLastSession.markdownDescrip: When a new chat opens, resume the most recent omp session (across all workspaces) instead of starting blank.
config.thinkingLevel.description: Thinking (reasoning) level applied after the agent starts.
config.approvalMode.markdownDescription:
Tool approval tier, passed to omp as `--approval-mode`. Also settable from the `access:` chip in the chat composer.

Note: approving a single `task` call hands its subagent the same tier, so an approved task can run shell commands without asking again.
config.approvalMode.enumDescriptions.0: Auto-approve reads; ask before writing files or running commands.
config.approvalMode.enumDescriptions.1: Auto-approve reads and file writes; ask before running commands.
config.subagentSubscription.markdownDesc: How much the extension subscribes to omp's subagent stream. `progress` reports each subagent's status, cost and current tool — the default, and what the board and the chat rows display. `events` additionally asks omp for the raw event stream, which nothing renders yet. `off` does not subscribe, and subagents stay invisible.
config.subagentSubscription.off: Do not subscribe — subagents are not shown.
config.subagentSubscription.progress: Status, cost and current tool for each subagent.
config.subagentSubscription.events: As above, plus omp streams the raw subagent events — no surface renders them yet.
config.theme.description: Accent palette of the chat panel. Applied live, without restarting the agent.
config.theme.enumDescriptions.1: Coral accent (#D97757), the original Claude Code palette.
config.accentColor.markdownDescription: Override the palette accent with a custom CSS color, e.g. `#8B7BF7` or `hsl(250 85% 72%)`. Empty = use `ompcode.theme`.
config.modelProfiles.markdownDescription:
Per-model behaviour profiles, layered on top of the built-in ones. Each entry is `{ family, match: { id?, provider?, host? }, contextFile?, badge?, runtime?, spawn? }`; `match.id` is a regular expression **as a string**. Your rows always win over the built-ins, whatever their specificity.

Only policy belongs here — omp already resolves the thinking dialect, the effort ladder, stream timeouts and tool-schema shape per provider, and overriding those makes things worse, not better.

Example — never let one model run shell commands unattended:

```json
[{ "family": "qwen", "match": { "id": "qwen" },
   "spawn": { "overlay": { "tools.approval": { "bash": "prompt" } } } }]
```
config.remoteRelayUrl.markdownDescriptio: Remote Control relay origin. Use `wss://` on networks; plaintext `ws://` is accepted only for a loopback self-hosted relay. The relay routes opaque end-to-end encrypted frames and cannot read the session.
config.worktreeBaseDir.markdownDescripti: Folder new workspace worktrees are created in. Empty = `<repo parent>/<repo name>.worktrees`, which keeps every worktree outside the repository so builds, watchers and `git status` in the main checkout never see them.
config.workspaceBranchPrefix.markdownDes: Prefix put in front of a workspace name to form its branch, e.g. `omp/` turns the workspace `feat-a` into the branch `omp/feat-a`. A prefix keeps agent branches recognisable and easy to sweep up later. Empty = use the name as the branch.
config.workspaceSetup.markdownDescriptio: What to do with a new workspace's setup commands — `setup` from `.ompcode/workspace.json`, or from a `.superset/config.json` the repository already has. A fresh worktree has no `node_modules`, no `.env` and no build output, so without setup the agent starts in a project that does not run.
config.workspaceSetup.enumDescriptions.0: Run setup as soon as the worktree exists.
config.workspaceSetup.enumDescriptions.1: Ask each time a workspace is created.
config.workspaceSetup.enumDescriptions.2: Never run setup; the workspace opens as-is.
config.portScan.markdownDescription: Scan workspace terminals for listening TCP ports and show them on the Sessions board.
config.portScanIgnore.markdownDescriptio: TCP ports the port scanner never shows.
config.reviewAutoRefresh.markdownDescrip: Recount a workspace's changes when its worktree is written to. Off, the Review view only recounts when you refresh it — quieter on a huge repository, at the cost of numbers that lag behind the agent.
config.orchestratorTools.markdownDescrip:
Give the main chat the tools to run workspaces itself: create one on a named model, wait for it, read its diff, merge the one that won, delete the rest. On, one sentence — "try this on GLM and on Sonnet, then show me both diffs" — is the whole instruction: the chat cuts the worktrees, starts the agents, waits, and reports back. Off, workspaces stay something you drive by hand from the `Sessions` view; nothing already created is affected.

A workspace's own agent never receives these tools, whatever this is set to — a worker that could create workers would fork worktrees until the disk filled. The tool list is declared once, at agent startup, so changing this restarts the running agents.

What this runs on your machine: `workspace_verify` executes the command the repository itself declares — `verify` in `.ompcode/workspace.json`, otherwise its `test`, `check` or `build` script — or another npm script the chat names, inside that workspace's worktree, with the editor's own environment and with no approval prompt. The chat cannot compose a shell command of its own; a workspace agent that edits `.ompcode/workspace.json` can, however, change what that declared command is.
config.costLimitPerWorkspaceUsd.markdown: Stop a workspace's agent once its session has spent this many dollars. 0 = no limit.
config.costLimitPerSessionUsd.markdownDe: Refuse new work once the orchestrator and all its workspaces together have spent this many dollars. 0 = no limit.
config.orchestratorMaxWorkspaces.markdow: How many workspaces the chat may keep at once. `workspace_create` refuses past this number, naming the limit and this setting, so a model that keeps starting workers instead of finishing them runs into a wall rather than into the disk: each workspace is a full checkout on disk and a metered agent in memory. Workspaces you created by hand count too. Raise it only if the machine can carry that many builds at once.
